model: snail at the pace of the fastest snail ever timed (33 cm in 2 min, Guinness), never stopping; Gus walks 3 mph, 0.70 m steps, sleeps 8 h; ocean = New York to London great circle; tap = 1 drip/s of 0.25 mL into a 40-gallon tub

facts_with_sources.record: Guinness World Records, 'Fastest snail racing': a snail named Archie (trainer Carl Bramham) covered the 33 cm (13 in) course in 2 min 00 s at the World Snail Racing Championships, Congham, Norfolk, 1995. Same figures in the 'Snail racing' encyclopedia article (0.006 mph).
facts_with_sources.walking: Usual walking pace of healthy adults: 1.31 m/s (Murtagh et al., Sports Medicine 2021, meta-analysis); 3 mph = 1.34 m/s.
facts_with_sources.ocean: Great-circle distance JFK to LHR: 5,540 to 5,567 km (3,442 to 3,459 miles) depending on the calculator; computed here with the haversine formula.
facts_with_sources.tap: USGS Water Science School, drip calculator: 0.25 mL per drip, 15,140 drips per gallon, 4,000 drips per litre.
facts_with_sources.hitching: USDA APHIS: hitchhiking snails 'can attach themselves to almost anything including shipping containers and can survive for months'; US Customs and Border Protection regularly finds live snails in air passengers' luggage (Houston 2021, Detroit 2023).
